# Nayasamuṭṭhāna (Ne 36)

**ID:** Ne 36
**Section:** Netti (ne)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nayasamuṭṭhāna* ("Molding of the Five Guidelines") constitutes the third major subsection of the explanatory section (*Paṭiniddesavāra*) of the *Nettippakaraṇa* [Caudron 2000; von Hinüber 1996]. The section presents and systematizes the five interpretive guidelines (*naya*)—namely *sīhavikīḷita*, *tipukkhala*, *nandiyāvatta*, *disālocanā*, and *aṅkusa*—which together with the sixteen modes (*hāra*) form the core hermeneutical method of the text [Balasooriya et al. 1980; Lopez 1988; Caudron 2000; Sen 2014]. In this section, each method incorporates verses from the preceding summary section, mapping basic root terms (*mūlapada*) to their doctrinal meanings and ultimate purpose, such as leading different types of audiences to liberation [Balasooriya et al. 1980; von Hinüber 1996; Sen 2014]. Specifically, *sīhavikīḷita*, *tipukkhala*, and *nandiyāvatta* structure mappings across sets of four, three, and two terms, while *disālocanā* establishes conceptual equivalences between unprofitable and profitable terms (representing suffering and the path), and *aṅkusa* operates horizontally [Sen 2014]. Oskar von Hinüber notes that the term *samuṭṭhāna* draws on Vinaya terminology and observes that the sequence and selection of *mūlapadas* here differ loosely from those listed in the earlier *Niddesavāra*, being illustrated directly through suttanta quotations [von Hinüber 1996].

 DharmaNexus also aligns passages with Northern Buddhist parallels, including Sanskrit texts (*Arthaviniścayasūtra*, *Dharmasaṃgraha*, *Saṅgītisūtra*), Chinese Āgama sutras (T1 and T12), and Tibetan translations such as the *Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa* and the *Abhidharmakośopāyikā* [DharmaNexus].
